record.original_question: Let Omega ⊂⊂ C^n be pseudoconvex with smooth boundary. For K ⊂ Omegā compact, let K̂ := {z ∈ Omegā; φ(z) ≤ supK φ, φ continuous on Omegā, φ plurisubharmonic on Omega}. Assume K̂ ∩ ∂Omega = K ∩ ∂Omega. Then Omegā has a Stein neighborhood basis.

evidence.quote: Problem 7.6.1 Let Ω ⊂⊂ Cn be pseudoconvex with smooth boundary. For K ⊂ Ω̄ compact, let K̂ := {z ∈ Ω̄; φ(z) ≤ supK φ, φ continuous on Ω̄, φ plurisubharmonic on Ω}. Assume K̂ ∩ ∂Ω = K ∩ ∂Ω. Then Ω̄ has a Stein neighborhood basis. -N. Sibony, sibony@anh.matups.fr Plurisubharmonic Functions 8.1 The Complex Monge Ampere Operator

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \Subset \mathbb{C}^n$ be a pseudoconvex domain with smooth boundary. For a compact set $K \subset \overline{\Omega}$, define the plurisubharmonic hull
$$\widehat{K} := \{\, z \in \overline{\Omega} : \varphi(z) \le \sup_{K} \varphi \text{ for every } \varphi \in C(\overline{\Omega}) \text{ that is plurisubharmonic on } \Omega \,\}.$$
Assume that for every compact $K \subset \overline{\Omega}$ one has
$$\widehat{K} \cap \partial \Omega = K \cap \partial \Omega.$$
Prove that $\overline{\Omega}$ admits a Stein neighborhood basis, i.e., there is a decreasing sequence of open Stein neighborhoods $\{U_j\}$ of $\overline{\Omega}$ with $\bigcap_j U_j = \overline{\Omega}$.
artifact.category_tag: Several complex variables / Stein neighborhood bases
artifact.status_search_result: Related results are known: Sibony established that smooth pseudoconvex domains satisfying property (P) (or having boundaries of class C^3 in certain settings) admit Stein neighborhood bases, and subsequent work by Harrington and others extended this to C^1 boundaries and to domains admitting plurisubharmonic defining functions. However, no direct reference confirming a complete solution of this precise conjecture (Stein neighborhood basis under the stated hull condition K̂ ∩ ∂Ω = K ∩ ∂Ω) was located, so the precise status remains unclear.

status_evidence.title: Property (P) and Stein neighborhood bases on C1 domains
status_evidence.snippet: Sibony has shown that Ω possesses a Stein neighborhood basis when the boundary is of class C³; an alternative characterization shows this holds for C¹ boundaries.
status_evidence.claim: Partial results exist (Sibony, Harrington) under additional hypotheses such as property (P) and boundary regularity, but no direct confirmation of the exact stated conjecture.

status_evidence.title: A note on plurisubharmonic defining functions in C^n
status_evidence.snippet: If Ω admits a smooth plurisubharmonic defining function on ∂Ω, then the closure of Ω admits a Stein neighborhood basis.
status_evidence.claim: Sufficient conditions yielding Stein neighborhood bases are known under various plurisubharmonicity assumptions on defining functions.
